record.field: Waste Management

Waste Management permissions are split in two: Operations (waste work rights) and Company Governance (administrator rights). Assign both sections when a user must run waste operations and administer their company.
Operations

Waste management rights: manifests, containers, worksheets, configuration, and related operational access. Combine roles as needed (e.g. Manager + Finance). Super Admin includes every operational role and also implies Company Administrator.
Company Governance

Administrator rights: company contacts, company records, and user creation within allowed companies. Select only one level. Pair with Operations roles when the user also performs waste work (or assign Super Admin under Operations, which already implies Company Administrator).
WMZ Backend User
Technical base role. Grants internal (backend) login. Automatically included with any Waste Management role — do not assign manually.
Operations Manager
Operations: manage waste service requests, schedules, worksheets, fleet, and operational workflows for the assigned company.
Admin Clerk
Operations: service requests, containers, pickup points, configuration clerical work, and related waste-management tasks.
Driver

Operations: field driver access for assigned manifests, worksheets, and mobile/driver workflows. Pair with Vehicle Inspection → Inspection User on the user form (applied automatically when Driver is selected).
Finance
Operations: billing, invoicing, tariffs, and financial records linked to waste services.
Service Provider
Operations: external or internal service provider managing assigned waste operations.
User Manager
Operations: create and manage backend users via Waste Management → Users. Usually combined with Company Administrator under Company Governance, or included automatically via Super Admin.
Super Admin

Operations: full waste-management rights — all operational roles, configuration menus, and Company Administrator (via implied groups). Use for a company manager who runs the full waste operation and administers their own company. Restrict Allowed Companies to one company for customer organisations (POPIA).
Company Backend Access
Governance: basic backend access for one company — view and edit company-scoped contacts and records within allowed companies. Does not include full operational or Contacts app menus on its own.
Company Administrator

Governance: administer one customer company — create branches, manage backend users (roles, passwords, logins), Contacts, and company records within their own company only. Pair with Operations roles when the user also performs waste work, or assign Super Admin under Operations which already implies this role.
Central Administrator
Governance: multi-company administrator for Zakheni head-office staff overseeing several customer companies. Assign only the companies they may access under Allowed Companies.
